Cemetaries are ideal campgrounds.

I should add that in Boy Scouts we did have a camp out in a cemetary once, and it was one of the best campouts we had. The nice larger cemeteries really are great, and you camp in the 'undeveloped' (unused) part of it, which is just like any park.

The grounds are well cared for, And well planned out. Most of the plants are chosen for low maintenance and to have a minimum of insect life, so people who don't like bugs (like me) don't have to bother with them as much. They are designed to be peaceful and relaxing, like a campground, except they have a lot more money than campgrounds.

Also, if you are on the run, cenotaphs and open buildings also provide great protection from the rain. They are usually made of concrete, so the wind protection can be perfect too. There are far worse places to hide than a cemetary. And most importantly of all, anyone who happens to see you will probably ignore you, despite trespassing on private property, as long as you don't look like a grave robber. That's very valuable when you need to get some sleep for the night.

But anyway, if you want to camp there, get the cemetery's permission, they may even have a designated campground. If you are on the run and need somewhere to hide, dont take a tent; just use a cenotaph or memorial building or whatever. Or get a hotel, but those were way too expensive for a broke college student.
